text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike detected for model 'rwd-base-3' in us-west-2 (serving-pool-22). SLO breach (p99 > 800ms). Paging eng-oncall. Correlation: recent kernel compile path rollout (trt-flashattn v2.1) at 11:42 UTC.

maria: saw this on the dashboard — p95 up to 210ms, p99 around 1.2s for streaming responses. Streaming stalls spikes coincident with page-in logs.

jonathan: confirmed. Traces show long waits in `kv_cache_fill` and syscall wait time rising. Looks like paging from CUDA driver during decode.

siva: @jonathan can you paste a flamegraph or trace id? I want to see if it's kernel-level vs user-level backpressure.

jonathan: trace id `trace-20260314-1145`

jonathan: snippet from trace:
```
# top of slow span
decode_step -> assemble_attentions -> trt_flash_attn_forward (kernel_launch) -> cudaMemcpyAsync(wait) -> sleep (page-in)
# p99 dominated by kernel_launch latency which correlates with v2.1 kernel build
```

clare: I see increased page faults in node logs too: `/var/log/syslog` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid` messages aligned with the spike window.

maria: customer impact: two paying customers on Dedicated had 5-10% of requests hitting p99 during the window; one reported streaming stalls in slack (support ticket #CS-4129).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260314-102. Priority: P1 (SLO breach). On-call: maria. Handoff scheduled at +30m if unresolved.

maria: immediate mitigation candidates: 1) roll back TRT/FlashAttention v2.1 to v2.0 on affected pool, 2) pin to older compile flags that disable `--fast-kernel` optimization, 3) route streaming traffic to fallback CPU pool temporarily. Thoughts?

siva: rollback TRT patch seems quickest. We should check risk of correctness regressions but v2.0 was stable for weeks.

kai: I'm spinning up a canary rollback on pool-17 now to validate. `deploy-bot` will show status.

deploy-bot: deploy started for package `trt-flashattn:v2.0` -> serving-pool-17. ID: d-44231.

jonathan: while that's going, can we reduce concurrency to avoid triggering page-ins? Maybe decrease `batcher.max_seq_per_worker` and throttle large streaming sessions.

clare: lowering concurrency is low-risk. I'm applying a temporary autoscale cap on pool-22 to reduce tail queueing. Command: `rbacctl scale --pool pool-22 --max-workers 12`

maria: doing that now. Will also enable KV prefix caching for long-running sessions to avoid repeated page-in of kv blocks.

(5m later)

deploy-bot: deploy d-44231 to pool-17 completed; health checks passed.

kai: rolled back on pool-17, traffic routed gradually. Early signals: p99 on pool-17 back down to ~280ms.

maria: good. Need to roll back pool-22 and pool-22-batch next. @siva can you coordinate rollback windows with infra? We should do canary then full roll.

siva: on it. Planning rolling rollback across 3 waves with 2-min steady-state checks.

jonathan: logs during canary show `cudaHostRegister` latencies spike prior to `kernel_launch` failure. That points to newer compile flags enabling host-pinned optimizations that trigger page faults on certain setups.

clare: I'm preparing a checklist to revert compile flags: remove `--enable-pinned-kv`, revert `-O3` override, and use `--compat-sm70` fallback. Will post commands in playbook.

maria: also open a ticket to infra/driver to investigage Xid counts — could be driver/firmware interacting with new kernels.

(25m later)

deploy-bot: rollback wave 1 completed on pool-22-batch. Wave 2 started.

maria: monitoring SLIs. p95/p99 trending down across affected pools. P99 now ~420ms cluster-wide, still above target but improving.

incident-bot: Note: Support notified customers with potential impact: CS-4129, CS-4132. Template sent.

siva: after full rollback, we need a root-cause branch: reproduce with the v2.1 kernel + `--enable-pinned-kv` on a perf test with long streaming sessions and small-seq tokens to trigger paging. If we can reproduce, open a PR to disable that flag by default.

jonathan: agree. I'll instrument more telemetry around host-register and page-fault rates and add guardrails to runtime to detect and fallback when page-fault rate > 0.5% over a minute.

maria: rollbacks finishing now. Final wave completed.

deploy-bot: rollback d-44231 waves complete. All pools reverted to `trt-flashattn:v2.0` and previous compile flags.

maria: p99 steady at ~230ms across pools. Streaming stalls resolved on sampled traces.

clare: creating post-incident checklist: coordinate with driver team to check firmware, run targeted perf runs, add automatic rollback rule to canary if p99 increases by >50% in 10m.

maria: I'll keep the incident open for a 2-hour monitoring window, then schedule a postmortem with Eng Runtime + Infra + Driver teams. Tagging: @siva @jonathan @clare @kai.

jonathan: one more thing — we should update the deploy checklist to prevent `--enable-pinned-kv` going out without canary on mixed GPU hardware. Add hardware compatibility gating.

siva: agreed. I'll draft the gating PR.

incident-bot: INC-20260314-102 status: mitigated (SLO restored). Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC.

maria: thanks team. I'll update CS with final impact once we have numbers from query logs.

clare: preliminary impact: ~0.8% of total requests in window hit p99 > 800ms, two customers saw visible stalls. We'll include exact counts post-query. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)
